title: Company-wide policies and processes: Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendor, Travel, Templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document centralizes Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard processes for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended for all employees, managers, and vendors who operate on Redwood systems or manage Redwood resources.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood corporate systems, cloud accounts, on-prem infrastructure, customer-facing environments, and vendor engagements. Where a stricter team-specific policy exists (e.g., SGX-stamped private deployments), that policy supplements — but does not replace — these baseline rules.

Owners & contacts
- Policy owner: finance-legal (primary), security-and-compliance (co-owner for security-related sections), people-ops (travel & templates).
- Document steward: Aisha Patel (people-ops) — aisha.patel@redwood.ai
- Escalation contacts: Security on-call: sec-oncall@redwood.ai, Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai, Legal: legal@redwood.ai

1) Access & Permissions

Goal: Ensure least-privilege access, clear ownership, and rapid provisioning while maintaining auditability.

Principles:
- Principle of least privilege: Grant only the minimum permissions required for a role or task.
- Time-bound access: Approvals for elevated or emergency access must include an expiry.
- Role-based assignments: Prefer role/group assignments over individual broad permissions.
- Auditability: Every privileged grant must be logged with approver, justification, and duration.

Standard processes:
1. Access Requests
   1) Submit request via Internal Access Portal (IAM ticket type). Include justification, required resources, and intended duration.
   2) Manager approval required for initial access. For privileged requests (admin, billing, production), SRE or Security approval also required.
   3) Provisioning team (eng-infra) completes assignment and documents ticket with permission changes.

2. Privileged Access (temporary elevated permissions)
   - Maximum default duration: 8 hours. Requests >8 hours require a business justification and security review.
   - All privileged sessions must use approved methods (short-lived credentials, Bastion + session recording, or SSO with MFA).

3. Periodic Access Review
   - Quarterly owners-run review: team leads receive an auto-report of active permissions and must re-approve or revoke within 14 days.
   - Critical roles (finance, production ops) require monthly review.

4. Service Accounts and Keys
   - Service accounts must be named with team prefix: svc-<team>-<purpose>. Rotate keys every 90 days; store secrets in approved secret store (HashiCorp Vault / cloud KMS).

Approval matrix (short table)
- Request type | Approver(s) | Max default duration
- Standard access | Manager | 90 days
- Privileged/production access | Manager + Security/SRE | 8 hours (default)
- Billing/financial access | Manager + Finance | 30 days

2) Change Management

Goal: Minimize customer/user impact from planned changes and provide rapid, auditable rollback paths.

Scope: All changes to production services, infra, networking, and customer-facing configuration. Routine non-production changes should follow lightweight review practices.

Change categories:
- Minor (no customer impact, low risk): Can be implemented during business hours with peer review.
- Major (potential customer impact, mid/high risk): Requires RFC, change window, and rollback plan.
- Emergency: Implemented to address active incidents; post-change RCA and formal retro required.

Change procedure (major changes):
1. Submit RFC in Change Management system with: purpose, owner, rollback plan, monitoring playbooks, and test plan.
2. Impact analysis by SRE & Product — include required SLO targets, estimated downtime, and mitigation.
3. Schedule change window with stakeholders and post status page template.
4. Pre-change checklist: run pre-flight tests, backup critical artifacts, snapshot databases where applicable.
5. Execute change with a designated change lead and observer. Record timestamps and significant events.
6. Post-change verification: run smoke tests, validate SLOs, and monitor for at least two times the expected stabilization window.
7. Close RFC with summary and lessons learned.

Emergency changes:
- Must be tagged as EMERGENCY and include a postmortem within 72 hours. Emergency approvals may be provided by on-call SRE or engineering director; documented approvals are required.

Change windows & freeze periods:
- Regular maintenance window: Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC (low-traffic window).
- Feature freeze: 7 days before major public releases or scheduled sales events.

3) Data Management

Goal: Ensure confidentiality, integrity, and availability of corporate and customer data.

Data classification (baseline):
- Public: non-sensitive marketing and product collateral.
- Internal: company-internal docs not intended for public release.
- Confidential: financials, personnel records, customer metadata.
- Restricted: customer PII/regulated data, keys, secrets.

Storage & handling rules:
- Restricted data must only be stored in approved environments with encryption-at-rest and in-transit.
- Use customer-specific VPCs/Private deployments for regulated workloads; personal devices are not allowed to store restricted data without MDM and encryption.
- Backups: all critical datasets must have automated, encrypted backups with retention policy defined by data owner.

Retention & deletion:
- Corporate documents: default retention 7 years unless legal or regulatory requires otherwise.
- Customer PII: retention set per contract; implement secure deletion process when TTL expires.

Data access & approvals:
- Access to Confidential/Restricted data requires data owner approval and a documented purpose. All access is logged.

Data breach procedure (high-level):
1. Detect & contain: notify security via sec-oncall@redwood.ai.
2. Triage: determine scope and affected systems.
3. Notify stakeholders: legal, communications, affected customers (per contract).
4. Eradicate & recover: remove root cause and restore from clean backups.
5. Post-incident: produce incident report, update policies and controls.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Goal: Provide clear, auditable processes for spending, procurement, and vendor contracting while enabling teams to move quickly.

Procurement thresholds & approvals:
- <= $1,000: Team lead approval.
- $1,001–$25,000: Procurement + finance approval (PO created).
- > $25,000: Procurement + finance + VP-level approval and legal review.

Process highlights:
1. For hardware, software, or cloud commitments, submit purchase request via Procurement Portal with business justification and budget code.
2. Procurement creates a PO and manages vendor communications. No spend should occur without an approved PO except in emergencies (see emergency spend below).
3. Expense reimbursements: submit receipts within 30 days via Expense system. Non-compliant expenses may be denied.

Emergency spend:
- Team lead + Finance approval required; Procurement must be notified within 48 hours to retroactively open PO or contract.

Preferred vendors & discounts:
- Procurement maintains a list of preferred vendors and negotiated discounts. Check Procurement Portal before engaging new vendors.

5) Vendor Management

Goal: Ensure vendor risk is managed, contracts are reviewed, and vendor access is safe and monitored.

Vendor onboarding checklist:
1. Business case and scope of work.
2. Security questionnaire and attestation (filled by vendor).
3. Legal contract review and SLAs.
4. Data handling addendum if vendor will access Confidential or Restricted data.
5. Technical onboarding plan, access accounts, and termination process.

Access rules for vendors:
- Vendors are always provisioned with the least privilege and time-limited credentials.
- Vendor accounts are labeled vendor-<company>-<purpose> and require an assigned Redwood sponsor.

Periodic vendor reviews:
- Annual risk review for vendors with access to Confidential/Restricted data or critical infra.
- Contract renewals must include updated security attestations.

Termination & offboarding:
- Procurement triggers vendor access revocation on contract end. Technical teams must remove vendor accounts and keys within 24 hours of termination.

6) Travel Policies

Goal: Provide safe, compliant, and cost-effective guidelines for business travel.

Booking & approvals:
- All travel must be pre-approved via Travel Portal. Managers must confirm purpose and budget code.
- Preferred providers and travel agency must be used for bookings to enable duty-of-care.

Allowable expenses & caps:
- Domestic airfare (economy), international (economy/business for flights >8 hours with manager approval).
- Lodging: up to $250/night standard in major metros unless pre-approved.
- Meals: per diem caps set by region in Travel Portal.

Health & safety:
- Duty-of-care: people-ops maintains traveler registry and emergency contact procedures. Travelers must complete pre-trip risk assessment for high-risk regions.

Expense reporting:
- Submit itemized receipts within 14 days of travel end. Out-of-policy expenses require manager justification and may be denied.

7) Internal Templates & Standard Forms

Purpose: Provide standard templates to accelerate consistent work and compliance. Templates are maintained in the Confluence templates library. Key templates include:
- Access request form (Access Portal link)
- RFC / Change Request template
- Vendor security questionnaire (Vendor Onboarding)
- Procurement request & PO template
- Travel pre-approval and expense report templates
- Data retention & deletion request form

Template governance:
- Template owners (procurement, security, SRE, people-ops) must review and approve template changes quarterly. Templates must include instructions, required fields, approver lists, and example entries.

8) Training & Compliance

- Mandatory annual training: Security basics, Data handling, Procurement basics for approvers.
- New-hire checklist includes access onboarding, expense system setup, and travel policy orientation.

9) Exceptions & Risk Acceptance

- Exceptions must be submitted to Risk and Exceptions board (security-and-compliance) with a compensating controls plan and an expiry date. Approvals are stored in the Exceptions register.

Appendices
A. Contact matrix
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai
- Finance: finance@redwood.ai
- Legal: legal@redwood.ai
- Security: sec-oncall@redwood.ai
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai

B. Quick checklists (for day-to-day use)
- Onboarding an external contractor: sponsor request -> security questionnaire -> limited IAM -> contract -> 30/60/90-day review.
- Making a production change: Submit RFC -> Stakeholder review -> schedule -> run pre-flight -> execute -> validate -> close RFC.

C. Change window calendar & freeze schedule (link to calendar): /confluence/policies-and-process/change-windows

D. Record retention table (summary)
- Financial records: 7 years
- HR records: 7 years post-employment unless otherwise required
- Customer contracts: contract-specified; default 7 years
- Audit logs: 1 year online; archived up to 7 years

Document update history:
- 2026-03-01: Initial published baseline (A. Patel)
- 2026-03-04: Minor clarifications to procurement thresholds and access review cadence

Review: This document will be reviewed annually or following any material incident affecting data, access, procurement, or vendor management.

Related policies: access-and-permissions (eng-infra), incident-response (oncall-and-incident-response), third-party-risk (security-and-compliance), travel-guidelines (people-ops).

Notes: This page provides the baseline company-wide requirements. Teams should supplement with team-level procedures (stored in team-specific Confluence spaces) but must not reduce the controls defined here.
